Read-only: never starts Fusion, never signs anybody in or out.

verbs.name: fusion_activate_document
verbs.summary: Make a named open document the ACTIVE one before driving it. EDIT and most modelling verbs act on whatever is active, so in a batch with several documents open this is how you stop a verb landing in the wrong file (page issue #47). Prefer passing expectDocument on the verb itself, which fails closed instead of merely re-targeting. An electronics design's schematic, board and 3D view are separate tabs with ONE name (type unknown): the reply says so in sameNameDocuments, and fusion_show_schematic / fusion_show_2d_board / fusion_show_3d_board {documentName} reach a specific view.

verbs.summary: Attach more footprints to a component (the standard's add_models): each becomes another device of the EAGLE component (Fusion's several-packages-per-component), pins joined by pad number; a model's footprint in another .lbr (pcblib) is copied in first. A footprint already attached is skipped (alreadyAttached), so it is safe to repeat. params, comment and description go on the component. Offline, preflighted.

Read back from the board; every change undone on a mismatch. Length, matched, diffpair and polyconnect rules have no class equivalent and are refused.

verbs.name: fusion_add_symbol_art
verbs.summary: Draw a chip's outline artwork into a component's symbol (the standard's add_symbol_art), offline in a .lbr: the polylines adom-symbol baked into the KiCad symbol, the KiCad body rectangle mapped onto the EAGLE symbol's own body box, as lines on the symbol layer, so the Fusion symbol shows the same chip as KiCad and Altium. clear (default) removes earlier art first, keeping the body's edges. Preflighted before writing.

verbs.summary: Is the AdomBridge add-in loaded and answering inside Fusion? Reports addinReady, port and version, plus busy when a long command holds the main thread. If Fusion is running but this says not ready, the add-in was installed while Fusion was open - Fusion loads add-ins only at launch - so call fusion_restart_for_addin (ask the user first when one is present).

verbs.name: fusion_apply_fusion_update
verbs.summary: Readiness EXECUTOR (Rust port, Phase 3): click Fusion's update offer IN THE BACKGROUND when auto-update is on (sticky pref; fusion_set_auto_update). Never the exit-class buttons while a host op is active. Answers {applied, button, why}.

Parts not yet smashed are smashed first. Each pick is made with only the target's layer displayed, so a pad or wire is never taken instead, and the board's layer display is restored. verbs.summary: Remember the browser+profile that authed to Autodesk so every later sign-in reuses it (power users have many browsers/profiles; the OS default is usually the wrong one). Call after a driven sign-in succeeds.

verbs.summary: Set the org's APS (PKCE) client id used for cloud search. Public identifier, no secret.

verbs.name: fusion_aps_signin
verbs.summary: Open the Autodesk sign-in in the REMEMBERED browser+profile (not the OS default); a background listener captures the token. Pass {exe,profileDir,name} to use+remember a specific browser, or {allowDefaultBrowser:true} to fall back to the OS default. If nothing is remembered, returns needsExtensionOpen so the caller opens authUrl in the user's real browser via nbrowser_open_window.

verbs.name: fusion_aps_status
verbs.summary: APS state: configured, signed in, token live, never-charge meter. When configured:false the hint sends you to your org's shared app ID on the wiki (adom-wiki settings get <org> autodesk-aps) before anything else; the fusion-aps-org-setup skill covers new boxes and first-time orgs.

verbs.name: fusion_aps_upload
verbs.summary: Upload a local file as a NEW cloud file (free Data Management; needs data:write scope). ⛔ FOLDER HYGIENE: NEVER pass a project ROOT folderId - the bridge REFUSES it (refused_root_upload). Loose files in a shared root clutter the team's cloud. Create/choose a real subfolder first (fusion_aps_create_folder under an 'Adom AI Workspace' folder), or just use fusion_make_3d_package / fusion_build_library_3d which auto-target a non-root workspace. To RELOCATE an existing file, MOVE it (preserves its urn) - do NOT delete + re-upload (mints a new urn, breaks 3D bindings). See the fusion-cloud-hygiene skill.

verbs.name: fusion_aps_versions
verbs.summary: Full (uncapped) version history of a file.

verbs.name: fusion_assembly_bom
verbs.summary: Structured, kit-aware MECHANICAL bill of materials for the active Design assembly (the counterpart to the electronics-only fusion_export_bom). Recurses organizational subassemblies but counts a physical part or a purchased kit/unit ONCE, so hardware modeled inside a kit (a '... with fasteners' bracket, a bearing/pulley) is NOT double-counted the way a flat allOccurrences walk counts it. Matches Fusion's Manage -> BOM quantities. Optionally writes a CSV.

input.panelMm: [w, h] when it ships in a panel

verbs.name: fusion_assembly_check
verbs.summary: Ready for JLCPCB assembly (the standard's assembly_check)? The board against both JLCPCB PCBA tiers as published (Economic and Standard): size, thickness and layers, parts on one or both sides, the smallest package and finest pin pitch, fiducials, and the BOM lines with no LCSC number (from the board's own part attributes); answers the cheapest tier every rule allows. The shared checks engine on the live board.

verbs.name: fusion_attach_3d_package
verbs.summary: LOW-LEVEL primitive: attaches ONE model to ONE package. Prefer fusion_create_library with parts[]. Attach a real 3D chip model to a library package, end to end: opens the .lbr (library active), runs Electron.Create3DPackage to enter the Package3DEnvironment showing the footprint, imports the STEP + auto-orients it flat on the footprint, then executes Package3DStop (FINISH). This BINDS the 3D onto the deviceset (Content Manager shows the 3D nested under the package; the Packages 'Package' column flips Placeholder->part-name). ONE desktop-side step remains: Fusion pops a modal Save dialog (an OWNED popup) - the response _hint gives the exact desktop_ui_click to confirm it. AFTER: re-grab desktop_screenshot_window and check ownedPopupCount for errors; the 3D preview LAGS a beat before showing the real chip. Both paths (filePath/modelPath) are WINDOWS paths - stage from the container first.

verbs.name: fusion_auto_classes
verbs.summary: Net classes from the nets' own names (the standard's auto_classes), from the shared checks engine: GND, Power (VCC, VDD, 3V3, VBAT...), Clock, HighSpeed (USB, Ethernet, HDMI, PCIe, DDR, MIPI, LVDS, SATA...) and the differential pairs their names spell. A proposal first; apply:true writes the classes that carry a rule (Power's width, powerWidthMm) as Fusion net classes through fusion_add_rule. Fusion pairs nets by their names, so the pairs need no writing.

input.lockPreroutes: bool, default true (Fusion's autorouter always keeps existing tracks)

verbs.name: fusion_autoroute
verbs.summary: Fusion's autorouter on the given nets, or on every net with unconnected copper. Existing tracks are kept (read back, or the run is undone); Fusion's DRC runs before and after. Refused before anything runs when a copper layer in use is switched off in the board's autorouter setup (Fusion would stop to ask): the reply names the layers.

input.deviceset: optional str (defaults to the library's first)

verbs.name: fusion_bind_library_3d
verbs.summary: LOW-LEVEL primitive: binds ONE STEP onto one deviceset. Prefer fusion_create_library with parts[] (which handles one part or many through a single path); reach for this only when you are driving a single bind deliberately. The CORRECT library in ONE call (the Library button's real bar: the 3D chip renders in the Content Manager preview): mints the part's 3D as a cloud f3d (make_3d_package), injects the wip_urn binding into the .lbr ON DISK (packages3d + package3dinstances), and reopens the library. Needs a signed-in Fusion session - the one cloud-dependent step in the wiki-to-EE circle. Autodesk's thumbnail preview lags ~2-3 min behind a fresh mint. NOTE: distinct from the older fusion_build_library_3d (multi-part batch pipeline).

input.outputDir: optional folder on this machine for bom.csv + bom-jlcpcb.csv

verbs.name: fusion_board_bom
verbs.summary: The bill of materials from the live board's own part attributes: one line per MPN with designators, quantity, value, package, manufacturer and the Mouser, DigiKey and LCSC numbers, plus the JLCPCB form (Comment, Designator, Footprint, LCSC). Board-only parts (test pads) are listed as such, and any part missing a distributor number is named. Read-only; with outputDir it also writes bom.csv and bom-jlcpcb.csv there.

verbs.summary: Board furniture in one call (the standard's board_features): mounting holes (bare, or plated via-holes on a net; at points or the four corners), fiducials (a filled copper circle and its mask opening), keepouts (Fusion's restrict layers) and a stitching-via grid on a net, each spot clear of other copper, pads, holes and the edge. Read back; a mismatch undoes it.

verbs.name: fusion_board_info
verbs.summary: Raw board geometry XML (copper/arcs/lines) for the open board.

verbs.name: fusion_board_outline
verbs.summary: Report the board edge the fab gets. Fusion's edge is its Dimension layer (20) and its Gerbers export it as the outline, so there is nothing to draw: this says how many outline items are there and whether they close. Change the shape with fusion_set_outline.

verbs.name: fusion_board_report
verbs.summary: One shareable page for the board (the standard's board_report): every check the shared engine has, run on one bundle of the live board and its companions (stack-up, pours, rules, 3D bodies, a fab record, the schematic's parts and netlist), with Fusion's own DRC and a picture of the board, written as one self-contained HTML file on the Fusion machine. A section missing its input says which. Fusion stores its DRC result in the board (the document then reads as modified): drc:false skips it.

Then fusion_new_electronics_from_eagle imports it as a linked schematic and board.

verbs.name: fusion_board_stackup
verbs.summary: Read a board's PHYSICAL fabrication stackup (see the pcb-stackup skill): copper layer count + copper/dielectric thicknesses from the EAGLE design rules (layerSetup/mtCopper/mtIsolate) plus the measured FR4 extent. A PCB is Cu/prepreg/Cu/core/.../Cu - the FR4 is NOT one slab. Use to build the stackup table + real-thickness exploded 3D view, and put a stackup table on every exported board's wiki page.

verbs.summary: One-screen summary of the open board (the standard's board_summary), shaped from one fusion_read_board round trip: the board (name, outline), its components with footprint, value, position and side, counts top and bottom, nets, the copper layers in use and addressable, layers carrying primitives, and the rule counts. raw:true answers read_board unshaped.

verbs.name: fusion_bodies
verbs.summary: Each part's 3D body as a box, from the design's 3D PCB: footprint rectangle in the board frame (x0, y0, x1, y1 mm) and height range above the surface it sits on (z0 standoff, z1 top; below the board for bottom parts). Names the parts with no 3D model (noBody) and the ones whose body is not where the board puts the part (suspect: off its footprint, floating or sunk, from a wrong library model or a 3D PCB not yet updated). The tallest part per side. What a height or enclosure check reads. Switches the design to its 3D PCB and back to the 2D board inside Fusion; takes no window or mouse.

Footprint pad names must match the netlist's pin numbers (R1.1 = pad 1 of R1). Coordinates mm, Y up.

verbs.name: fusion_build_library_3d
verbs.summary: Build a RENDERING multi-part 3D library in ONE call - the whole programmatic pipeline. For each part it makes the footprint+chip f3d package (no GUI dialogs, optional before/after screenshots) and collects the wip_urn, then injects ALL bindings into the combined .lbr in one pass (no hand XML surgery) and opens the finished library once. A part minted before on this machine and account, with the same model, footprint, placement and destination, reuses its 3D package when its cloud file still exists (reused:true on the part, partsReused and partsMinted in the reply; freshMint:true, on the call or a part, makes it again). This is the verb for a basic-parts sampler / any many-part library; it replaces the per-part make_3d_package loop + manual binding. projectId/folderId default to the MAIN-project upload folder. Each part is independent, so re-run just the failed parts if Fusion resets mid-run.

verbs.name: fusion_cancel_run

output.stage: str at the time of the request

verbs.summary: STOP a library import that is in flight (fusion_install_library_bundle / fusion_create_library) - the user's escape hatch from a long run, wired to a Cancel button in web control. Cooperative, not a kill: the run finishes the part it is on (a STEP import cannot be interrupted mid-command without leaving a half-made design, up to ~60s), keeps every 3D package already minted and binds them into the library, closes its scratch documents, and leaves the library open in Fusion (not saved to the cloud). The run then reports stage:cancelled, verdict:cancelled, errorCode cancelled_by_user, cancelledAt (which stage) and how many parts were done, on the same fusion_prove_result poll the caller already makes; cancelRequested:true shows on the very next poll before the boundary is reached. Omit runId to cancel the latest run still in flight. Idempotent; a run that already ended answers alreadyFinished.

The 3D before/after shots don't show these. Requires the .lbr OPEN in the Electronics Library workspace (fusion_open_lbr first). verbs.summary: Change existing pours in place: the pen width (the narrowest copper the fill can reach; a pen wider than a throat leaves it empty) and the isolation. Each pour is named by net, layer and outline, picked on the midpoint of its longest edge, then RATSNEST refills. The readback proves each pour took its new width/isolate and that no track or via changed, and reports the filled area before and after.

input.vias: [{x, y, drill?, diameter?}] mm: the vias at these points

verbs.name: fusion_check_clearance
verbs.summary: Part-to-part clearance (the standard's check_clearance), from the shared checks engine on the live board and fusion_bodies: courtyard mode compares part boxes (pads and 3D bodies) on the same side; pads mode compares pad copper of different parts sharing a copper layer, by its real outline. verbs.name: fusion_check_dialogs

verbs.name: fusion_check_orientation
verbs.summary: Advisory (the standard's check_orientation): 2-pad parts whose rotation could be better, each orthogonal turn scored in place by airline length (a routable net's MST with the pad there; a plane-like net's distance to its nearest pad); parts whose best turn saves minImprovementMm are listed. Nothing moves: the shared checks engine on the live board.

verbs.name: fusion_check_recovery
verbs.summary: Ask whether a cloud file has a crash-recovery document waiting, which would raise Fusion's recovery modal on open. BEST-EFFORT: Fusion's Python API does not reliably expose this (apiReliable reports whether the property existed), so a false negative is possible; the dependable signal is an open that times out, and fusion_dismiss_blocking_dialogs clears the modal. Finds the file by exact name in one project folder.

input.profile: optional str (browser profile to name in the sign-in hint, e.g. edge:me@work.com)

verbs.name: fusion_claim_seat
verbs.summary: Make THIS machine the active Fusion seat, the first-class way to move a licence between boxes while testing. Starts Fusion if needed, then answers Autodesk's 'Active Sessions Exceeded' modal in the BACKGROUND (Continue): this box takes the seat and the other machine's Fusion suspends RESUMABLY, keeping its documents. Answers needs_signin (never a credential prompt) when the box is not signed in: run fusion_signin first. Confirms with fusion_account and reports the account and licence it ended up with.

verbs.name: fusion_cleanup_cloud_files
verbs.summary: PRECISELY delete a list of cloud files by lineage urn - SAFE cleanup of AI-created clutter. Deletes ONLY the exact fileIds given (never name-guessing), so it can't touch a teammate's file in a shared folder. Loops server-side. Get the ids from fusion_aps_browse (item .id). Use this to remove f3d files the bridge created. A big list takes minutes (relay may time out at ~60s while deletes continue server-side - re-browse to confirm).

verbs.name: fusion_cleanup_libs

verbs.name: fusion_create_library
verbs.summary: ONE-CALL library creation for web-control (one call = one consent). EVERY LIBRARY IS MULTI-PART - a single-part library is simply parts:[one entry], and there is no separate single-part verb to choose. Pass parts:[{package, lbrPath, modelPath}] for any number of parts; the older {libraryPath, stepPath} shape still works and is normalised into a one-element parts list, so both run the identical code path and the ETA scales with the part count either way. TWO entry shapes: A) {libraryPath, stepPath} - a ready .lbr plus the 3D; B) {kicadSymbolPath, kicadFootprintPath, stepPath, pinMap?} - KiCad sources; needs adom-lbr, which is Linux-container-only by platform rule, so on Windows/Mac boxes shape B refuses IMMEDIATELY (adom_lbr_unavailable, before any staging or Fusion launch - fusion_readiness reports kicadIngest up front). Convert at AUTHORING time in a container and use shape A. pinMap = explicit {pinName: padName} for when pin numbers do not match pad names (BGA-style). Chains convert -> bind 3D -> prove (four evidence frames + verdict) in the BACKGROUND and returns immediately; poll fusion_prove_result (stage narrates; top-level `verdict` proven/not_proven is the score - `stage:done` only means the chain finished). EVERY PART IS PROVED, not just the first: a 10-component library streams 40 evidence frames, FOUR per component (symbol, footprint, 3d, ganged) in assembly order, each tagged with `part` so a front end can group them as they arrive, and `provedParts[]` reports per-part pass/fail. The library is proven only if EVERY part is - one good part does not vouch for nine unchecked ones. On the FINAL fetch pass {inlineFrames:true} to get each evidence frame as a base64 thumbnailDataUrl a browser can render (plain polls return box paths only). The chain closes its library document on success AND failure - batches need no between-part sweeping. stepPath is required for a PROVEN library - no real 3D body without it.

verbs.name: fusion_demo
verbs.summary: FIRST-TIME-USER DEMO in one verb - the thing to run when someone new wants to SEE what this bridge does (HD's installer calls this). Takes them from nothing to a real board: launches Fusion, FINISHES the Autodesk sign-in - it OPENS the sign-in in the user's NATIVE browser IN THE BACKGROUND (never interrupting their work) and returns signinWhere/signinProfile/signinSession so you can tell them exactly where it is waiting, then offer three paths: they finish it, you foreground it, or (with their OK) you drive it. Native browser via ABE/nbrowser_* because that profile is already signed into Autodesk - never pup, which is anonymous, sets up APS cloud search (or explains it if declined) and runs a LIVE sample search so they see 2-second results, then opens an electronics PROJECT and walks SCHEMATIC -> 2D BOARD -> 3D BOARD, screenshotting each view to show them. STAGED + RESUMABLE: every call advances as far as it safely can and returns stage/done/narrate/screenshots plus a _hint with the exact next action; keep calling it until done:true. NEVER leave a first-time user parked on the sign-in screen - that is the failure this verb exists to prevent. See the 'fusion-demo' skill. TOUR MODE: pass {mode:'tour'} for the ASYNC guided ELECTRONICS tour (John, 2026-09-04: Adom is an electronics prototyping company, so the tour shows electronics, never a mechanical part): eight beats over the bundled sample part - the library, the symbol, the footprint, the 3D chip minted from its STEP and bound into the user's hub, then a REAL board from the user's hub (BQ25792, the Adom charger; args.board or args.boardUrn override) in schematic, 2D board and 3D board, falling back to a generated solo board only when the hub has none, and a cloud search; multipart libraries are mentioned in the narration, never shown (a bind is minutes per part). Captions are 32px on one line so they never cover the remote. ab's glass remote (desktop_demo_panel id fusion-tour) drives it: play, pause, next, back, mute, unmute, X = stop, with an instant loopback callback plus a poll backstop, one FIFO for the panel and fusion_demo_control, an ack caption per press; captions narrate every beat and pre-rendered narration audio plays locally (mute is session-only, unmute replays the beat). Every beat is measured before it moves (front, title, painted, stable) and then moves (2D zoom through the add-in, 3D orbit and zoom through Fusion's camera, verified by capture). Returns {demoId, estimatedSec, steps} at once; fusion_demo_progress {demoId} carries step, beatIndex/beatCount, percent, paused, muted, stopping, panel, presses[], captions[], per-step verified/placed/foregrounded/motion, shots[] (one evidence frame per beat), windowsRestored and tourDocsClosed. Fusion is placed on 80% of the primary work area for the show and restored at the end. Pass legacy:true for the previous step-list tour.

LIVE EVIDENCE (issue #30): each frame MAY carry stepShot {step, title, image} - a ~640px base64 capture the BRIDGE took at that step's completion, one per step, riding the first frame after it completes (render these during the run; the page should not guess-snap). shots[] streams too: mid-run it carries paths for every completed step; pass imagesAs:base64 + sinceShot:<count you have> to receive only NEW shots fully encoded. done:true = the full gallery (base64 by default). verbs.name: fusion_export_optimized_glb
verbs.summary: Fusion board -> wiki-grade optimized GLB. Exports STEP, the EAGLE .brd (board:true) and optional silkscreen and submits them to service-step2glb molecule mode (anchor to MP pins + silk bake + gold pins + join/weld/prune + Draco; with the board it also writes <stem>_footprint.json and <stem>_symbol.json beside the GLB, and <stem>.web.glb when the model is over the wiki inline budget). The reply carries the molecule-publish gates (gates.pinSize/pinSizeSource/footprintApplied/footprintPins/footprintRebase/warnings) and its _hint names any gate that is not met. Every export also writes <stem>-fab.zip (Gerber + mixed-plating Excellon + .gbrjob from the bundled JLCPCB CAM job) and export.json (tool and version, exporter version, every source file with sha256 and role including each file in the zip, and the stackup from the Gerber job), per board-look EXPORTERS.md. Nothing in the STEP or the Gerbers is renamed: ~465KB/~31 draw calls vs a raw ~16MB/~25000 that halts the viewer. Bounded-waits `wait`s (default 90); small boards return complete, big boards return {pending, jobId} - finish with fusion_fetch_optimized_glb. Use for a component page's component.parts.model_3d. STACKUP RULE (John 2026-07-15, see pcb-stackup skill): board bbox = the FR4 body, NEVER the whole assembly (components overhang edges + tower above); each overlay goes at ITS layer's z (copper at FR4-top, silk above mask); copper traces are REAL 35um 3D bodies colored like the FR4 - recolor them + translucent mask in the RAW GLB before optimizing to make routing visible; put the measured stackup table on the board's wiki page. PUBLISH EVERYTHING: a board's wiki page repo must carry EVERY exportable design file (.f3d/.step/.usdz/EAGLE .brd+.sch/Fusion .fbrd+.fsch/gerbers/BOM/CPL/GLBs/renders), not just the 3D - the page exists to share the design.

verbs.name: fusion_install_library_bundle
verbs.summary: COMPOSITE, the Fusion twin of kicad_install_library_bundle (#68): ONE call takes a staged Cloud Library bundle (zip of <Lib>.lbr + <Part>.step models, or a bare lbrPath with STEPs beside it), unpacks it safely, places it under ~/Documents/Adom Libraries/<name>/, pairs EVERY deviceset with its STEP by name (deviceset, package, normalised, prefix; a one-part library pairs its single model regardless), lints part numbers (partMetadata: MPN, manufacturer, Mouser/DigiKey/LCSC - reported, never blocking), pre-flights Fusion state (fusion{status}), and starts the same bind -> prove chain fusion_create_library runs. ASYNC BY CONTRACT: returns IMMEDIATELY with runId + statusVerb because a STEP bind is 3-15 minutes and cannot fit a relay window; poll fusion_prove_result (measured percent, four streamed proof frames per part, provedParts[], and an addin_restart_required payload the CALLER turns into the ask). PARTIAL SHIPS: a deviceset with no model is a NAMED skip in unbound[], the rest still bind; partsBound < partsTotal is the signal. Each part is minted on its own single-deviceset library (the Package3D generator loads the FIRST package of the open library, so a merged library would put every chip on part one's footprint), with the STEP placed exactly as published (orient:false, origin trusted), then all urns are bound into the merged library, and after prove the bound library is SAVED TO THE CLOUD under <project>/Adom Libraries so it appears in Fusion's Library Manager (cloudLibrary{saved, fileId, duplicatesBefore} in fusion_prove_result). Per-part scaffolding is deleted; the user is left with one library plus its per-package f3d folder. capture:false only places the files and returns. This is the one contract the wiki CLI (`library install --format fusion`) and the Export button both read; the recipe has one owner.

This is THE verb for 'make a board with these new parts on it'; fusion_make_test_project is the one-part circuit variant. After it: fusion_show_2d_board / fusion_show_3d_board {capture:true}, fusion_schematic {action:"show"}, fusion_save_to_cloud. NO cloud, NO sign-in, no pre-existing content. After it, fusion_show_schematic / fusion_show_2d_board / fusion_show_3d_board all work on the result. verbs.name: fusion_managed_library_create
verbs.summary: Create a NEW managed library on library.io FROM the library in front (which must already be saved in a Fusion Hub). Drives MANAGE > LIBRARY.IO > Push, then completes Fusion's Create Managed Library dialog. PITFALL: a managed library created under one Autodesk account is NOT visible to another account until its managed FOLDER is shared on library.io - proven live, so do not assume hub membership shares it.

verbs.name: fusion_managed_library_link
verbs.summary: Link the library IN FRONT to an existing managed library on library.io. With no name, opens Fusion's Select Managed Library picker, returns its rows as records (name/type/version/managedFolder/description) and CANCELS - a safe read-only listing of what this Autodesk account can reach. With name, selects that row and confirms. SAFETY: after linking, Fusion offers to force-update your library FROM the managed one; 'Replace Local Library' would destroy your parts, so this verb answers CANCEL by default - pass onUpdatePrompt to choose deliberately. A managed library owned by ANOTHER Autodesk account does NOT appear until its managed FOLDER is shared with this account on library.io; being in the same Fusion hub is not enough.

verbs.name: fusion_managed_library_pull
verbs.summary: Pull the newest version FROM library.io into the linked library in front. A pull ends in ONE of two CEF dialogs and BOTH block the add-in until answered: the force-update prompt when content differs (answered MERGE by default, since pull is an explicit request for the managed content - pass onUpdatePrompt:'replace' to overwrite local parts entirely, or 'cancel' to back out), or 'Up to Date' when already current. If neither appears, nothing was pulled and this reports failure rather than a false pass - Fusion greys Pull out on a library that was never linked.

verbs.name: fusion_managed_library_push
verbs.summary: Push a NEW VERSION of the library in front up to its linked managed library on library.io. Clicking the menu item alone does NOT push: Fusion raises a CEF 'Create New Version' confirmation and THAT is what creates the version, so this verb completes it and fails with confirm_missing rather than reporting a false pass. On a library that is not linked yet, Fusion offers Create Managed Library instead and this reports not_linked_yet - use fusion_managed_library_create. NOTE: Library Manager keeps showing the IMPORTED version number after a push, so the row gains an update-available badge instead of incrementing.

verbs.name: fusion_managed_library_unlink
verbs.summary: Unlink the library in front from its managed library on library.io. Fusion greys this out on a library that was never linked, so a silent no-op there is expected.

verbs.name: fusion_mcp_call
verbs.summary: Call any tool on Autodesk's Fusion MCP server (fusion_mcp_read, fusion_mcp_update, fusion_mcp_execute, fusion_mcp_electronics_read). The bridge handles the MCP streamable-HTTP handshake for you (initialize -> MCP-Session-Id -> notifications/initialized) and re-establishes a dropped session automatically. MCP acts on the ACTIVE Fusion document, so open one first. PREFER a native fusion_* verb when one exists - they are tested here and return richer hints - and reach for MCP for Autodesk's text-to-CAD surface.

verbs.name: fusion_mcp_enable
verbs.summary: Turn Autodesk's Fusion MCP server ON by driving Fusion's Preferences dialog for the user. Autodesk exposes NO API for this toggle, so the UI is the only route: this opens Preferences (Commands.Start PreferencesCommand), expands General, selects API, ticks 'Fusion MCP Server (runs locally on this device)', then clicks Apply and OK. Needs Fusion running; briefly uses the foreground and announces why with an on-screen caption. NEVER ask the user to do this by hand first - do it for them, then tell them it is handled. Note the setting is DISCARDED if Fusion is killed or restarted before Apply is clicked.

verbs.name: fusion_mcp_resources
verbs.summary: List Autodesk MCP resources, or read one by uri. These are mostly the Electronics entity schemas (resource://mcp.electronics_schema_*) that describe what fusion_mcp_electronics_read can return.

verbs.name: fusion_mcp_status
verbs.summary: Is Autodesk's Fusion MCP server up, and what does it expose? Autodesk + Anthropic ship a LOCAL MCP server at http://127.0.0.1:27182/mcp exposing Fusion's own text-to-CAD surface (read geometry, execute/update features, read Electronics design data). It binds LOOPBACK on the user's machine and was built for Claude Desktop running there, so a CLOUD AI cannot reach it at all - this bridge runs on that machine and proxies it for you. Returns enabled, serverInfo and the live tool list. OFF by default: if it reports enabled:false, call fusion_mcp_enable and the bridge turns it on for the user.

ray_cast.description: Cast batches of rays against named occurrences, without changing anything (assembly planning: what a part seats on, what blocks its way in, whether a tool reaches a screw). Each ray is cast against each occurrence it names, in that occurrence's own component coordinates, about a millisecond on a part, where a ray against a big subassembly's component (thousands of bodies) took a quarter of a second. Returns hits: a row per ray answered, [[occurrence index, distance in mm rounded to 0.01], ...], one entry per occurrence the ray meets within length (its nearest hit), nearest first; a ray that starts inside a body meets that body's exit face. Also cast (rays answered, in order), complete, missing (indexes with no occurrence at that path), failed (casts Fusion refused) and seconds. Not journaled: it stops at budgetSeconds or before its reply passes 1 MiB (stopped: budget|reply_bytes) and the caller sends the remaining rays. ray_cast.description: Cast batches of rays against named occurrences, without changing anything (assembly planning: what a part seats on, what blocks its way in, whether a tool reaches a screw). Each ray is cast against each occurrence it names, in that occurrence's own component coordinates, about a millisecond on a part, where a ray against a big subassembly's component (thousands of bodies) took a quarter of a second. Returns hits: a row per ray answered, [[occurrence index, distance in mm rounded to 0.01], ...], one entry per occurrence the ray meets within length (its nearest hit), nearest first; a ray that starts inside a body meets that body's exit face. Also cast (rays answered, in order), complete, missing (indexes with no occurrence at that path), failed (casts Fusion refused) and seconds. Not journaled: it stops at budgetSeconds or before its reply passes 1 MiB (stopped: budget|reply_bytes) and the caller sends the remaining rays. Requests over the CLI's argument limit (128 KiB) go in several calls.

budgetSeconds.description: Stop casting after this many seconds (default 30) so the reply comes back inside the relay's 60 s; the reply then has complete:false and answers the first `cast` rays. Send the rest in another call.

verbs.summary: Guarded main-thread parametric parts and assemblies: sketches, solid features, atomic parameter edits, component definitions/copies/placement, seven as-built joint motions and limits, rigid groups, interference, materials and assembly mass/center of mass, local supplier STEP/SAT import with SHA/provenance, native McMaster command, structured/flat BOM CSV, topology readback, health and safe exports. Geometry queries refuse ambiguous selections; root-space distance/angle measurements return witness points. Typed sketch trim/extend/split/break and signed modern offsets, reference-defined construction axes and native sketch constraint diagnostics are available through exact operation schemas. Regular geometry-solving joints, joint origins and native motion links have guarded typed operations, exact attachment/parameter readback and timeline restoration. Read-only configuration inspection and active-row BOM provenance are available; configuration lifecycle and configured-design model writes remain disabled pending native recovery/archive gates. Incomplete configuration scope also blocks complete BOM output. Typed model mutations use runtime-proven PTransaction recovery; transaction_probe verifies the backend (new_design does this automatically). Writes require sessionId,operationId and current target {documentId,revision}. Durable admission must commit before dispatch. Retry exact args with the same ID; query durable status after timeout. Old-session history is readable but never replayed. Storage failure after execution returns reconciliation-required, preserving available evidence without claiming rollback. References expire on model changes. Files/document lifecycle are outside model transactions.

verbs.summary: Import a legacy EAGLE .sch (+ paired .brd) into a NEW Fusion electronics design so the parts INSTANTIATE (schematic + populated board, lands in the PCB editor). The ONLY way to author a board from EAGLE source: Document.newDesignFromLocal opens the schematic editor but does NOT instantiate parts, and the Fusion-native .fsch/.fbrd container is opaque binary you can't build offline. This fires Fusion's own ImportSCHAndBRDCmd and drives BOTH native Open dialogs (the .sch then the .brd) in the BACKGROUND via desktop_ui_click by accessible name (no foreground). Stage both files to Windows first (send_files). After: fusion_show_2d_board, RATSNEST + 'AUTO ;' to autoroute, fusion_show_3d_board for 3D. PREFLIGHT (1.10.20): refuses with eagle_files_missing before touching any dialog when either file is not on the Fusion machine; if the Open dialog does not accept the file the bridge cancels the dialog itself (open_dialog_stuck), so nothing is ever left on the user's screen. Prefer fusion_schematic {action:"open"}, which picks this route only when a .brd exists next to the .sch. ASYNC by contract (1.10.22): returns {started:true, runId, statusVerb} at once and runs the dialog-driven import on the exe; poll fusion_eagle_import_status {runId}. The record and the final reply carry documentName, partsExpected (elements in the .brd) and partsPlaced (read back from the board); success needs parts on the board (nothing_instantiated otherwise). Pass wait:true only from inside the exe.

input.filePath: required str (.lbr WINDOWS path C:/...; stage from container first)

verbs.name: fusion_open_lbr
verbs.summary: Import an EAGLE .lbr library into Fusion's Electronics LIBRARY editor (Content Manager / Electronics Library workspace), not a PCB design. PITFALL: filePath MUST be a WINDOWS-local path (C:/...). The chip-fetcher/adom-lbr pipeline runs in the cloud container, and there is NO container-to-Windows push verb, so STAGE the .lbr onto Windows first (serve it on a proxied port + Invoke-WebRequest via shell_execute), then pass the C:/ path. PITFALL: an adom-lbr .lbr is 2D ONLY - symbol + footprint + a PLACEHOLDER 3D package; the real 3D chip is NOT attached (that needs a Fusion cloud URN). To attach the 3D, see the 'fusion-libraries' skill. Pass verify:true to round-trip-confirm Fusion parsed the deviceset, then check fusion_get_app_state (activeWorkspace 'Electronics Library').

input.filePath: required str (WINDOWS path to the .sch, C:/...; must exist on the Fusion machine)

verbs.name: fusion_open_schematic
verbs.summary: Open a LOCAL legacy EAGLE .sch in Fusion's Schematic Editor (dialog-free Document.newDesignFromLocal; a background open). NAV RULE: the schematic, 2D board and 3D board are VIEWS of ONE electronics design, not standalone files. For a team design open the DESIGN document (fusion_open_cloud_file / fusion_open_by_urn) and switch views with fusion_show_schematic; this verb is for a .sch that exists on the Fusion machine (push it there first). Drive the opened sheet with fusion_electron_run (WINDOW FIT, DISPLAY ALL). The bridge captures a post-open screenshot because Fusion can raise a blocking dialog the API cannot see.

input.name: the panel's title (case does not matter; part of it is enough); omitted, the list

verbs.name: fusion_panel
verbs.summary: Open one of Fusion's docked panels (the standard's panel), or list them: Browser, Inspector, Display Layers, Selection Filter, Design Manager, Place Components, Errors, Bill of Materials, Text Commands, Comments ... Fusion's Panels.List names them, Panels.Expose opens one and Panels.ValidateState proves it is expanded. Nothing takes the foreground.

verbs.name: fusion_panelize
verbs.summary: A manufacturing panel (the standard's panelize), planned by the shared checks engine: rows x cols copies, V-score lines or mouse-bite tabs drawn the way JLCPCB reads them, rails with tooling holes and fiducials, JLCPCB's panel rules checked. Fusion builds it as a NEW EAGLE board from the open board's source (copy k's parts and nets renamed _k, the copies' own outline left to the panel's rout path) and opens it as a local design; the board you panelized is untouched. dryRun returns the plan.

verbs.name: fusion_part_parameters
verbs.summary: The attribute names the design's placed parts carry, with how many carry each (the standard's part_parameters); with name, that attribute's value on every part.

input.name: footprint name filter (library form)
input.path: a .lbr on the Fusion machine (library form); omitted, the open board

verbs.name: fusion_pcb_report

output.data: {kind: library, components: [{name, pads, padsBboxMil, census, bodies}], bodyCols} | {kind: board, outlineMil, components: [{designator, footprint, pads, padsBboxMil, nets, bodies}], census, tracks, bodyCols}

verbs.summary: Numbers instead of pixels (the standard's pcb_report). For a .lbr (path), every footprint (or the ones name matches): its pads, the pads' bounding box in mil, a census of its primitives (smd, pad, wire, circle, polygon, text, hole ...) and its 3D packages. For the open board (no path, or want:'board'): the outline in mil, each part with its pads, nets and pad bounding box, the copper census and the tracks.

input.names: optional [str] component names to measure (default all)

verbs.name: fusion_physical_properties
verbs.summary: Per-component physical properties (volume cm3, mass kg, density, area, center of mass) for the active design. Reads them directly so BOM/costing tools no longer have to run getPhysicalProperties inside a modeling script. Pass names to scope to specific components.

verbs.name: fusion_pin_pad_check
verbs.summary: Do the footprints fit their symbols (the standard's pin_pad_check)? Part by part, the symbol's pin numbers (fusion_schematic_data) against the placed footprint's pad names on the board: pins with no pad, pads with no pin, and parts only on the sheets or only on the board. The shared checks engine.

input.caps: [ref] (default the caps on its power nets)
input.gapMm: cap to IC box, default the engine's

verbs.name: fusion_place_decoupling

output.placements: [{cap, net, pin, powerPad, x, y, rotation, side, padToPinMm, from}]

verbs.summary: Plan decoupling capacitors beside an IC's power pins (the standard's place_decoupling), from the shared checks engine: each cap gapMm outside the IC's box on the side of the power pin it serves, turned so its power pad faces the pin, slid along that side when the spot is taken; the plan is checked with placement_check. A plan: moveArgs is fusion_move_parts' arguments, boardId and expectedRevision included.

input.parts: [{library, footprint, ref?, value?, x, y, rotation?, side?}] mm (required)

verbs.name: fusion_place_parts
verbs.summary: Footprints from a .lbr onto a board with no schematic (the standard's place_parts), with position, rotation and side, read back. A board linked to a schematic is refused: Fusion takes its parts from the sheet (fusion_sch_place_part, then fusion_move_parts).

input.vias: required [{net, x, y, diameter (mm, default 0.6), drill (mm, default 0.3)}]

verbs.name: fusion_place_vias
verbs.summary: Add vias at exact points (stitching, thermal, escape): VIA per via with its drill and diameter, then read back.

verbs.name: fusion_placement_check
verbs.summary: Review the placement before routing (the standard's placement_check): parts whose courtyards (pads and 3D body, grown by marginMm) overlap on the same side, parts off or over the board edge, pads closer than edgeMm to the edge, and parts on a mounting hole: the shared checks engine on the live board and fusion_bodies (pads only, bodiesUsed:false, when the bodies cannot be read).

input.viaPerimeter: bool: a via at every perimeter stub

verbs.name: fusion_plan_fanout
verbs.summary: Plan a part's fanout (the standard's plan_fanout), from the shared checks engine on the live board and its stack-up: a BGA's outer ring escapes on the surface and each inner ball takes a dogbone via (or a via in the pad); a perimeter package's pads take an outward stub (a via at its end for ground, or with viaPerimeter); an exposed pad a via grid. calls are fusion_route_net arguments, one per net; conflicts lists vias and stubs that would come too close to another net's pad.

input.parts: optional [{package, lbrPath, modelPath}] - the parts you intend to import (drives the estimate)
input.stepPath: optional single .step when not passing parts[]

verbs.name: fusion_plan_library_import
verbs.summary: PRE-FLIGHT for a library import: does NO work and changes nothing. Reports whether Fusion is installed, running, or needs its add-in loaded (with a plain-language message you can show the user), plus a per-stage plan with MEASURED per-machine time estimates scaled to the number of parts you are sending - a multi-part library does one STEP import per part, which is the slowest stage, so the estimate grows with the library. Call this FIRST so the wiki can render the summary and the progress bar's steps, then run the import and poll fusion_prove_result, which reports the SAME stage names.

input.layers: [copper layer] default [F.Cu, B.Cu]; list them all (e.g. [F.Cu, In1.Cu, In2.Cu, B.Cu]) so a via is checked on every layer it passes
input.viaCost: a via costs as much as this many mm, default 5
input.widthMm: default the board's width rule, else 0.25

verbs.name: fusion_plan_route

output.planner: {algorithm, gridMm, layers, clearanceMm, edgeClearanceMm, widthFrom, viaFrom}

verbs.summary: Plan a path for one net between two pads on the live board without changing it (the standard's plan_route), from the shared checks engine (adom-eda-checks): a bounded orthogonal A* on any copper layers listed (default F.Cu and B.Cu), with through vias between them; pads by their real outline, the board's strictest copper clearance and copper-to-edge rule. Answered as routeNet, fusion_route_net's arguments (boardId and expectedRevision included), to pass on unchanged; found:false with a reason when no path fits. Pours are not obstacles: fusion_route_net undoes a route that cuts another net's pour in two. Fine-pitch pads need gridMm 0.1.

verbs.name: fusion_plate_vias

output.data: {holes: int, plated: int, fixed: 'Footprint:Pad;...', joinedToLands: int}

verbs.summary: Make every drilled hole in a library's footprints a plated pad (the standard's plate_vias), offline in a .lbr. In EAGLE a pad is always plated and an unplated drill is a <hole>, so each hole becomes a pad. A hole inside an SMD land (a heatsink via in an exposed pad) is named after the land (EP@2, EP@3 ...) and joined to that land's connect in every device, so it sits on the land's net; any other hole becomes H1, H2 ... and stays unconnected. The copper ring is left to the board's restring rules, as for any EAGLE via. Written with a .bak and preflighted; dryRun shows the plan.

verbs.name: fusion_pour_state
verbs.summary: Read every pour on the live board with Fusion's own computed fill, each with a stable id made from its net, layer and outline (Fusion stores none): filled area per pour, per layer and per net, and which pours were never filled (no RATSNEST since they were drawn). The measure step of the AI flow's Fusion lane.

input.set: optional {key: value}: the keys fusion_set_preference takes

verbs.name: fusion_preferences
verbs.summary: Read Fusion's own settings (theme, scroll direction, orbit scheme, orientation, length unit), or change them with set, live with no restart. The standard's preferences: fusion_get_preferences and fusion_set_preference as one verb.

verbs.name: fusion_preflight_lbr
verbs.summary: PRE-ANALYZE a .lbr: will Fusion open it? Offline and instant - no Fusion needed, nothing launched. Runs the named checks the bridge learned from real Fusion rejections: file-readable, size-sane (truncated-transfer corpse detection), xml-parses, root-is-eagle, packages-nonempty (Fusion's silent 'No Components'), symbols-present, devicesets-present (missing ones make EDIT raise Create-new prompts), connects-resolve (dead wiring renders fine and connects nothing). fusion_open_lbr and fusion_create_library run the same gate automatically; call this directly to gate a batch BEFORE staging.

input.save: optional bool, default true

verbs.name: fusion_prefs_close
verbs.summary: Apply+OK (save:true, the default) or Cancel Fusion's Preferences dialog. Settings changed via fusion_prefs_open are NOT persisted until this is called with save:true.

input.section: optional str (see knownSections in the response)

verbs.name: fusion_prefs_open
verbs.summary: Open Fusion's Preferences dialog and optionally jump to a section, then hand back a SCREENSHOT + shotId you can click in. This is how you reach ANY Fusion preference: the Python API exposes only a thin slice (theme/orbit/units, debuggingPort, developer tools) and everything else, including the MCP server toggle, is UI-only. Sections: general, api, design, manufacture, electronics, render, drawing, material, graphics, network, preview features. Child sections under General are lazily rendered by Qt and never appear in the UIA tree, which is why this returns an image to click rather than control names. ALWAYS finish with fusion_prefs_close {save:true} - nothing is saved otherwise, and killing/restarting Fusion first discards the change.

verbs.name: fusion_prewarm
verbs.summary: Warm the bridge ahead of the first real call, WITHOUT starting Fusion: confirms the add-in is synced into every Fusion add-in folder, readies the space-free staging folder, and caches the PCB design-rules catalog from adom/pcb-design-rules. Adom Bridge calls it once per installed version in the background (bridge.json prewarm.verb); safe to call again any time. Launching Fusion is never part of it.

verbs.name: fusion_progress
verbs.summary: The bridge's timing book (the standard's progress): the long operation in flight now with how long it has run and its usual time, the measured phase timings, per-verb run times (p50, max) and the most recent runs.

input.fabRules: a fab from adom/pcb-design-rules, recorded for later
input.name: the design's name (required)
input.parentDir: a folder on the Fusion machine (required)
input.title: str

verbs.name: fusion_project_create
verbs.summary: A new, empty electronics design (the standard's project_create): an empty schematic and board written as EAGLE source in <parentDir>/<name>/ (the board's copper count in its layer setup; title and text variables as the schematic's global attributes) and imported into Fusion as one design with its sheet and board linked, so a part placed on the sheet goes on the board (linked:true, about 30 s, through Fusion's own import in the background; Adom Bridge may ask for an OK, and then it answers stillRunning with a runId for fusion_eagle_import_status). If the import can't run, it opens the two files as unlinked documents and says why (linked:false, whyNotLinked). Save it to the cloud with fusion_save_to_cloud.

input.expectDocument: the design's name (default the document in front)
input.project: the same, in the standard's word

verbs.name: fusion_project_info

output.files: [{kind, name, open, saved, modified, path, version, modifiedAt}]
output.name: str

verbs.summary: A Fusion electronics design at a glance (the standard's project_info): its documents (the open ones and its cloud files of the same name: project, schematic, board, 3D PCB) with version and date, the sheet tree, the board (copper layers, parts, nets, size) and its net classes. Read only; the design must be open.

input.project: a .sch, .brd or the folder holding them, on the Fusion machine (required)

verbs.name: fusion_project_rename
verbs.summary: Rename a design kept as EAGLE files (the standard's project_rename): <name>.sch, .brd, .lbr and EAGLE's numbered backups become <newName>.*, and a folder named after the design is renamed with them. EAGLE files do not name each other, so nothing inside changes. Refused while Fusion has the design open. A Fusion cloud design is renamed in Fusion's data panel.

input.expectDocument: the design's name (default the document in front)
input.label: added to the folder name

verbs.name: fusion_project_snapshot
verbs.summary: A dated plain-file copy of a Fusion design (the standard's project_snapshot): a folder on the Fusion machine with the schematic and board as EAGLE XML, a PNG of every sheet and of the board, and PDFs made from them. Fusion's cloud versions stay as they are; save one with fusion_save_document.

input.runId: optional str (omit for the latest run)

verbs.name: fusion_prove_result
verbs.summary: POLL a background run started by fusion_create_library or the detached fusion_build_library_3d. Returns stage + stageLabel, plan[] with measured per-stage estimates, stagesDone, percent, etaSec, confidence, and evidence[] filling in AS EACH ARTIFACT LANDS (symbol -> footprint -> 3d -> ganged). For a 3D build it carries per-part progress (minting X (3/7)), partsDone/partsTotal and parts[] with each wip_urn. stage:done only means the chain FINISHED - the top-level verdict (proven/not_proven) is the score, and a run that captured zero frames lands stage:failed with blocked_by_dialog (carrying the dialog text) or no_evidence_captured rather than reporting done. Pass inlineFrames:true on the final fetch for base64 thumbnails a browser can render. restarts[] {at, why, kind} lists any restart the chain performed (only with allowRestart). prove.planned / prove.skipped say whether evidence frames were captured and why (AI threads bind only by default).

verbs.name: fusion_read_board
verbs.summary: The standard's read_board: the live board in one round trip, as sections: components, nets (with net classes), layers (copper and stack-up), copper (tracks, arcs, vias, pads, pours), rules, occupancy (layers in use) and outline. sections picks some (csv); limit caps each list, with the full counts beside it.

input.libraryPath: a .lbr on the Fusion machine (with name)
input.name: the package's name

verbs.name: fusion_read_footprint

output.name: str
output.pads: [{number, type, shape, at, sizeMm, drillMm, layers, rotation}]

verbs.summary: Every detail of one library footprint (the standard's read_footprint): pads with number, type, shape, position, size, drill, layers and turn; the layers used; the courtyard box (component exclude layers 39/40, else pads and placement outline); graphics per layer; the 3D packages that instance it. From a .lbr (libraryPath + name) or, by libId 'Lib:Name', from the libraries the open board embeds.

verbs.name: fusion_read_rules
verbs.summary: Every design rule on the live board from Fusion's rule manager, disabled ones included: name, kind (Copper Clearance, Minimum Copper Width, Teardrop...), enabled, priority, both scopes, value and preferred value, whether live and manual DRC check its kind, plus the classic design-rule values (params) and the rule set's name.

verbs.name: fusion_read_schematic
verbs.summary: Components of the open design's schematic (the standard's read_schematic), from fusion_schematic_data: designator, libReference (the deviceset), comment (the value), device, library and the part's parameters.

input.params: bool, default false: every attribute with its value
input.path: required: EAGLE .sch or Fusion .fsch on the Fusion machine (alias filePath, schPath)

verbs.name: fusion_read_sheet_file

output.complete: bool (false with hierarchical modules or unknown devicesets)

verbs.summary: Read a schematic straight from its file, without Fusion running: every part of an EAGLE .sch (or the .sch inside a Fusion .fsch) with its designator, library reference (deviceset + device), value, description, part number, library, sheet, position and orientation, parameters on request, and its pins: number (the pad), name, gate and electrical type (input, output, io, open_collector, passive, hiz, power, supply, not_connected) for a schematic review. Milliseconds. The saved file, not the live sheet.

verbs.name: fusion_read_symbol
verbs.summary: Read a component of a .lbr back (the standard's read_symbol): description, its pins with number, name, gate and electrical type (0 input, 1 io, 2 output, 3 open collector, 4 passive, 5 hi-z, 7 power), its attributes and its footprints (devices).

verbs.name: fusion_readiness
verbs.summary: FAST readiness check (does NOT launch Fusion): is the Fusion host app installed + running + the bridge ready to drive? ab DETECTS Fusion (never installs it) via bridge.json 'detect', and auto-installs Python if missing (ab >=1.9.47). Call this before driving Fusion; if installed-but-not-running, fusion_start. SELF-HEALS the seat/licensing dialog (background UIA + screenshot-verify) whenever it detects one. Pairs with ab's bridge_readiness.

input.save: optional bool (default false): save open documents before closing

verbs.name: fusion_release_seat
verbs.summary: Give up the Autodesk seat from THIS machine so another box can claim it with no modal at all: closes Fusion cleanly (documents are NOT discarded; an unsaved one refuses and says so) and leaves the account signed in, so this box can claim the seat straight back. The counterpart of fusion_claim_seat.

verbs.name: fusion_remove_footprint
verbs.summary: Delete a footprint from a .lbr (the standard's remove_footprint); refused while a component uses it.

input.layer: F.SilkS, B.SilkS, F.Fab, B.Fab, Edge.Cuts, a copper name or a Fusion layer number

verbs.name: fusion_remove_graphics
verbs.summary: Remove board-level graphics (the standard's remove_graphics): lines, arcs, rectangles, circles, polygons, texts and dimensions, by id, or every one on a layer and/or of a kind. Fusion stores no ids: an id is kind:layer:points, and a dry run lists them. Each is picked with only its layer shown; the rest of the board must read back unchanged, or every DELETE is undone. Graphics inside parts are not touched.

verbs.name: fusion_remove_items
verbs.summary: Delete tracks and vias given exactly as fusion_routing_state returned them (track start, end, layer; via position). The board is read back as the old one minus exactly those items, or every removal is undone. results[] is per item: ok or err:not found.

verbs.name: fusion_remove_parts
verbs.summary: Remove placed parts by designator (the standard's remove_parts). Fusion keeps the board in step with the schematic and ignores a part deleted on the board, so the part is deleted in the design's schematic and leaves the board with it. Each removed part lists the nets its pads carried; a locked part is refused unless allowLocked. Tracks that met its pads stay.

verbs.name: fusion_remove_pours
verbs.summary: Delete pours (all of them, or the ones named by id from fusion_pour_state, or by net, layer and outline) so a board can be poured again after a refine. Each DELETE picks the outline point farthest from every pad (refused if none is 1 mm clear), and the readback undoes everything if a part or a track changed.

verbs.name: fusion_remove_symbol
verbs.summary: Delete a component from a .lbr, and the symbols no other component uses (the standard's remove_symbol).

verbs.name: fusion_rename_footprint
verbs.summary: Rename a footprint in a .lbr (the standard's rename_footprint): every device that uses it and its 3D package instances follow.

verbs.name: fusion_rename_symbol
verbs.summary: Rename a component in a .lbr (the standard's rename_symbol).

input.outputPath: the image on the Fusion machine (default %TEMP%/adom-render/board-<side>.<format>)
input.renderSeconds: seconds before a high render is cancelled, default 45

verbs.name: fusion_render_board_3d

output.framed: {refs, missing, pivot, zoom} when refs was given

verbs.summary: A 3D picture of the board from one side (the standard's render_board_3d and render_board): Fusion's own view of the design's 3D PCB, saved as an image without the user's tab changing (it is put back). Fitted to the board, or framed on parts (refs, with marginMm), turned by rotate ('x,y,z' degrees about the view's centre, e.g. '-45,0,45'). quality high is Fusion's local ray-tracer from the same camera (every render setting put back; cancelled after renderSeconds). Orthographic by default; transparent background for png.

input.outputPath: the png on the Fusion machine

verbs.name: fusion_render_board_layers
verbs.summary: Chosen board layers as an image without a window (the standard's render_board_layers), through Fusion's EXPORT IMAGE: a preset (all, top_copper, bottom_copper, top_silkscreen, bottom_silkscreen, top_soldermask, bottom_soldermask, top_paste, bottom_paste, outline, drill, assembly_top, assembly_bottom, fabrication) or layers by the standard's copper names (F.Cu, In1.Cu .. In14.Cu, B.Cu) or Fusion's numbers; dpi, mirror, monochrome. png only: Fusion writes no svg, so format svg is refused by name.

input.drawingSheet: true (Fusion draws the frame as a part; false is refused)
input.name: file stem, default schematic (a baseline is per name and sheet)
input.width: int px, default 2000 (dpi is chosen from the drawn extent)

verbs.name: fusion_render_schematic
verbs.summary: Render a schematic sheet to a PNG without opening a window, through Fusion's own EXPORT IMAGE, and keep visual baselines: baseline set stores the render, baseline compare renders at the baseline's width and reports the pixel drift, the changed region (mm on the sheet) and a diff image with the changed pixels in red.

input.anchor: a ref from source (default the first)
input.source: [refs] of the placed channel (2 or more)
input.targets: [[refs], ...] each in the same order as source

verbs.name: fusion_replicate_layout
verbs.summary: Copy one channel's placement to matching channels (the standard's replicate_layout): each target keeps its anchor part where it is and every other part takes the source's offset and turn from the anchor, turned by the anchors' rotation difference; a bottom part stays mirrored. One guarded move (fusion_move_parts: read back, undone on a mismatch); footprintMismatches names parts whose footprint differs from their source part. dryRun returns the moves.

verbs.name: fusion_repour
verbs.summary: Refill every copper pour on the live board (Fusion's ratsnest pass, with hidden fills shown again) and read the poured copper back: filled area per layer and per net, pours that poured nothing, and each pour's fill.

input.force: optional bool default false - also discard MODIFIED Untitled docs

verbs.name: fusion_reset_workspace
verbs.summary: Bring Fusion back to a clean slate between runs: closes named documents AND the Untitled scratch the library/bind flow leaves behind (page issue #59). Fusion always keeps ONE blank document alive, so a single remaining Untitled is correct rather than a failure. MODIFIED Untitled docs are left untouched unless force:true, because those can hold real unsaved work.

verbs.name: fusion_resolve_seat_dialog
verbs.summary: Readiness EXECUTOR (Rust port, Phase 3): detect + resolve the Autodesk seat/licensing modal ('Active Sessions Exceeded' / 'Suspend Remote Session') in the background, at most 3 UIA clicks per call, screenshot-verified. Idempotent: nothing up answers clicks:0. fusion_readiness calls this itself when it sees the dialog; call it directly only when you are driving the launch by hand.

input.save: optional bool (default true) - save open documents before restarting

verbs.name: fusion_restart_for_addin
verbs.summary: ASYNC: returns immediately (started:true) and restarts Fusion in the background, SAVING the user's open documents first; poll fusion_readiness until ready with the new addinVersion (a restart takes 60-120s, longer than the relay budget; pass wait:true for the old blocking form). Finish add-in setup by restarting Fusion. Call this when any verb returns errorCode addin_restart_required (the add-in was installed/updated while Fusion was already open, and Fusion only loads add-ins at launch). A busy add-in (errorCode fusion_addin_busy, readiness addinBusy) is NOT a reason: it is loaded and working. ASK THE USER FIRST when a human is present - the failing verb's payload carries userMessage plus openDocuments/unsavedDocuments so you can show them what is open. Refuses with unsaved_named_document rather than discarding a never-saved document, and with restart_needs_decision (nothing killed or discarded) when Fusion asks to save work the bridge did not make; restartPolicy force (an AI-only machine) discards and kills instead.

verbs.name: fusion_return_path
verbs.summary: Signal tracks running over a gap in the neighbouring layer's reference copper, with a pour plan that closes each gap (apply as fusion_apply_pours): the shared checks engine on the live board, its stack-up and Fusion's pour fills.

input.gridMm: placement grid for the off-grid check

verbs.name: fusion_review_board
verbs.summary: Design-review checks over one read of the board (the standard's review_board), from the shared checks engine: thirteen checks, errors first; skipped and notImplemented name what was not judged. With the schematic's parts (fusion_schematic_data) for the checks that need them; the off-grid check runs only with gridMm.

verbs.name: fusion_ripup_nets
verbs.summary: Take whole nets' tracks and vias back up (RIPUP per net, one undo step each) so they can be routed again, wider or another way. Their pours stay. Readback proves no track or via is left on those nets and no pour was lost.

input.allowSplit: bool: keep a route that splits another net
input.clearance: mm, can only raise the board's rules
input.layer: the first copper layer, by name or number; default F.Cu
input.paths: optional list of paths instead of points
input.points: waypoints [x,y] or {pad} or {x,y,layer}; a waypoint's layer is the layer after it (a via where it changes)
input.viaDiameter: mm, default .6 (viaSize also works: fusion_plan_route's routeNet)

verbs.name: fusion_route_net
verbs.summary: Create explicit net copper in the live Fusion canvas, on any copper layer of the board (F.Cu, In1.Cu ... B.Cu, or EAGLE's numbers). Clearance preflight against pads by their real outline, tracks and arcs, vias, holes (footprint mounting holes too), footprint and board copper and keepouts (tRestrict/bRestrict), with board/revision guards and exact copper readback. Pours are repoured round the new copper; a route that cuts another net's pour in two is undone (splits_net) unless allowSplit. One or several paths per call; no general autorouting. Use routing_drc for native DRC.

verbs.name: fusion_route_pair
verbs.summary: Plan a differential pair routed as a pair (the standard's route_pair), from the shared checks engine: one centreline from the source pads' midpoint through waypoints to the destination pads' midpoint, each net offset to its side at width + gap (or the gap for diffOhms from the stack-up), with mitred corners. Answers routeNet [pos, neg] as fusion_route_net arguments, widthRule for fusion_add_rule and skewMm; problems lists crossings and other copper closer than the clearance, and while there are any success is false.

verbs.name: fusion_routing_drc

verbs.name: fusion_schematic

output.via: str: the verb that did the work

verbs.summary: START HERE for a schematic. ONE verb, three actions. action:"open" lands in the schematic editor from whatever names the design: fileName (+projectName) or urn or query for a CLOUD design (opens it, then switches to the schematic view), schPath for a local EAGLE .sch (its sibling .brd is imported with it so parts instantiate, unless withBoard:false; a .sch alone opens dialog-free), or filePath for a Fusion-native .fsch. action:"create" writes a blank EAGLE schematic on the box and opens it as a NEW local electronics design with the schematic editor active, no dialog anywhere. action:"show" switches the already-open design to its schematic view. Every reply says which underlying verb it used (via). Remember: a schematic is a VIEW of an electronics design, not a file of its own, which is why there is no verb called open_a_schematic_file. To put a library's parts on a NEW schematic and board for showing them off, use fusion_make_showcase_project instead.

verbs.name: fusion_schematic_plan
verbs.summary: Plan a grouped schematic from a netlist: one labelled frame per block, the block's parts in a row, every connected pin given a short stub named for its net and a label. Returns the command groups for fusion_schematic_run (one call per group, so the sheet grows block by block on camera). Pins may be named by pad (U1.3) or pin (U1.VIN). Pure computation from the .lbr; nothing in Fusion changes.

verbs.name: fusion_schematic_review
verbs.summary: Review the schematic (the standard's schematic_review), from the shared checks engine: every placed pin with its electrical type (fusion_schematic_data) against the netlist (Fusion keeps board and schematic in step). Errors such as power pins on no net and outputs driving each other; warnings such as inputs left open and single-pin nets.

input.libraryPath: required for ADD: the .lbr on this machine (its file name is the library name in ADD)

verbs.name: fusion_schematic_run
verbs.summary: Build a schematic live: a list of complete, non-interactive EAGLE commands run one at a time on the active schematic (ADD 'dev@lib' 'NAME' R0 (x y), VALUE, NET 'name' (pts), LABEL, WIRE, TEXT, LAYER, CHANGE STYLE/SIZE/WIDTH/RATIO, WINDOW FIT), with an optional pause between them so a viewer sees it grow. Anything else is refused before the first command runs. A list of any length: past 300 commands the bridge checks all of it first, then runs it in batches (batches; on a failure failedAt in your list, batchesDone). The call answers with the whole reply when it finishes within about 100 s; otherwise it answers stillRunning with a runId, and fusion_schematic_run {runId} polls until stillRunning is false, which is the whole reply. ADD is proven against libraryPath on disk first (the deviceset must be there; the library is USEd by the bridge), so the component picker can never open. A .lbr Fusion 2706 cannot ADD from (no line breaks between elements, a byte-order mark, single-quoted attributes, a 3D package naming a footprint the file does not have) is rewritten in place first, keeping its element tree apart from those dead 3D entries (libraryReformatted, library3dEntriesRemoved). The bridge sends USE itself, for the file named in libraryLoaded. Readback: the parts and nets on the sheet from a fresh export.

verbs.name: fusion_set_auto_update
verbs.summary: Turn AUTOMATIC Fusion updating on/off for this user. ON BY DEFAULT, and deliberately INVISIBLE: Fusion ships updates constantly and nags with an 'Update Now / Update Later' panel plus a '14 days until Fusion must update' countdown. Every fusion_readiness call checks for that offer and, if present, the bridge clicks it IN THE BACKGROUND (UIA, no foreground, no caption) so the download starts and the newer build comes up on the next launch. The user should never have to click it. Call with no args to read the current setting; {enabled:false} opts out and the choice is STICKY (~/.adom/fusion-bridge/prefs.json) - once a user opts out, NEVER click their update prompts again. Tell the user this is handled for them rather than asking them to update.

verbs.name: fusion_signin
verbs.summary: SELF-DRIVING as of 1.9.32: launches Fusion if needed, clicks Sign In, opens the OAuth in the right profile, TYPES THE EMAIL and advances to the exact remaining wall (password/2FA/handoff), toasting the user at that step only - see signinWall + _hint in the response, and the fusion-autodesk-signin skill. Sign Fusion in through the CORRECT browser profile - the fix for Fusion's dumb OAuth that fires at the OS-DEFAULT browser and lands in the wrong Autodesk account. Fusion opens its sign-in in whatever browser is default (e.g. a personal Chrome), but a user's Autodesk seat often lives in a different profile (work). This verb reads the FULL authorize URL (client_id/PKCE/state/request_id) that Fusion wrote into that wrong browser's HISTORY and re-opens it in the RIGHT profile IN THE BACKGROUND; the URL completes back to the running Fusion via the idmgr/callback + autodesk:// handoff, so the browser no longer has to be the OS default. Pass {profile:'chrome:you@work.com'} to fix + remember your Autodesk profile; else it probes each profile for a live Autodesk session (or asks). Staged: if Fusion hasn't opened the browser yet it returns stage:'click_signin' so you click Fusion's Sign In first. BEST: pass {auto:true} to run the WHOLE chain in ONE server-side call - it clicks Fusion's Sign In, polls the browser history on-box for the fresh authorize URL, and re-opens it in the target profile, all without extra remote round-trips, so it fits inside Fusion's ~2-min OAuth request expiry even on a slow/flaky relay (the manual staged path is the fallback). Fusion's request EXPIRES in ~2 min, so a stale captured URL returns stage:'stale' - restart Fusion (fusion_stop/start) for a fresh request and retry auto PROMPTLY. See the 'fusion-multiprofile-signin' skill.

input.code: required str (the 6 digits; non-digits are stripped)

Exists so you can finish a login END TO END for the user instead of parking them on a 2FA screen: if `adom-google` is available in your container, read the code out of their Gmail (`adom-google gmail search 'from:autodesk verification code' --limit 1`), pull the 6 digits, and call this. If adom-google is NOT installed, tell the user that installing it would let you automate logins like this, then let them type it. NEVER ask the user for a code you could read yourself. The bridge ALSO toasts the user's desktop whenever it hits a human wall, so you do not need to ask it to.
